These controls accompany individual triage of the Webshells and Laudanum
Debian archive members. `cases.json` records scan-visible assertions and
`evaluation_*` assertions for unions pruned by the engine's low-value
composite filter. Use `cleave test-rules` for those evaluation assertions.

PHP directory entry functions and iterator references moved from traversal
and inventory into directory listing; glob calls live under path search.
Indexed fread resources prove stream reads, not process creation or pipes.
Exact consumers were updated. The traversal union no longer treats a PHP
single-directory listing as recursive walking. Ransomware's legacy literal
"glob" module predicate excludes PHP, whose path-search call now has its own
structured capability. Other languages keep the existing predicate.

Inbound form methods and upload handling do not establish outbound HTTP
client operations. The controls retain a positive stream-context POST and
negative upload handler. Member facts distinguish live PHP password reads
from commented examples. Netcat documentation in C comments is not executed.

All seven targeted controls pass. The full validator also fails on the
pre-change revision with the installed engine (30 failed fixture checks).
Several failures require projections absent from available engine source,
including shell.literal_command_flows and composer.install_hook_flows.
The original test expectations remain intact. The Flowcrafter score cap
increases by one to account for its newly notable PHP listing capability.
